newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields off, extend low volume rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields off, extend low volume rally.

text.p: Australian bond yields were lower as the market continued Thursday's low volume rally with this week's corrective sell-off now seen completed.
A late short-covering rally in U.S. Treasuries helped to give domestic bonds their early positive tone, but a lack of local data will again keep interest low key, traders said.

Expectations of another easing in monetary policy after the Reserve Bank board meeting on July 1 should see the market keep its current positive tone and September bill futures are all but pricing in such a move at 94.88, indicating a cash rate of 5.12 percent. Current official interest rates stand at 5.5 percent.

Yield spreads to the U.S. continued to head back towards the lows seen earlier this week, but lost ground against Canada, which rebounded with the Canadian dollar on Thursday. New Zealand debt yields rose slightly, but trade was light ahead of next Thursday's budget and RBNZ's monetary statement on Friday.
